page: Vultr vc2-1c-1gb is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the Cloud Compute line, designed around shared-resource allocation. It delivers one shared vCPU powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, paired with 1.0 GB of memory and 25 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for instruction sets including AES, AVX, BMI2, and FMA. There are no discrete GPUs attached, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place the vc2-1c-1gb consistently in the lower performance brackets due to its single shared vCPU and minimal memory footprint. The PassMark CPU test recorded a score of 1061.65, while stress-ng measured 691.39 for single-core execution. Memory throughput tests show 7.8 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 5.19 GB/sec for large block writes. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 1.0 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 0.95 GB/sec.

Given its minimal capacity, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for lightweight tasks that do not justify dedicated hardware or large RAM overheads. However, the 1.0 GB memory ceiling and shared single core make it unsuitable for data-intensive services, parallel builds, or concurrent database queries. The vc2-1c-1gb serves as a practical host for basic development, low-traffic static websites, background automation, and lightweight monitoring agents.
